title: enterprise bundle verify --json
description: `enterprise bundle verify --json` (bundleVerifyResult, internal/cli/enterprise_bundle.go). Read-only: it runs every apply check (anchors, key, signature, manifest, tenant, device group, platform, version floor, minimum product version, file hashes, inline secrets, secret references and, on a managed device, credential presence and signed values, the config validator and the effective policy digest) and changes nothing. On a managed device it also lists the credentials the device lacks (secret_refs_missing) or stores with a value the bundle does not sign (secret_refs_mismatch) and predicts whether the apply restarts the gateway (restart_prediction). As root on a managed device the floor includes the confirmed bundle; otherwise a floor_unchecked warning says only the anchor min_version was checked. Exit 0 when ok; 1 (Linux, macOS) or 1603 (Windows) for a refusal; 2 or 1639 for invalid arguments (errors[0].code invalid_arguments).

result.description: already_applied: the bytes are the current confirmed bundle: apply writes no new receipt and re-installs the bundle config only when the installed config.yaml drifted from it (config_drift true; restart_prediction says whether that restarts the gateway).

floor.description: The version a bundle must exceed.

floor_source.description: What sets the floor (enterprisebundle.FloorSource): none, the anchor file's min_version, the last confirmed bundle, or both at the same version.

secret_refs_missing.description: Names (never values) of the secret_refs credentials this device does not hold, required and optional, in manifest order; [] when every one is stored. Present only on a managed device whose credential store could be read for every reference (root or SYSTEM); absent off a device, when the store could not be read (warning secret_presence_unchecked) and on a refusal before the credential check. A secret_ref_missing refusal lists every missing name, so the agent stores them all (enterprise secret set) before it verifies again. Absent on builds before 1.0.3.

secret_refs_mismatch.description: Names (never values) of the secret_refs credentials this device stores with a value the bundle does not sign (value_sha256), required and optional, in manifest order; [] when every stored one is the signed value. Present exactly when secret_refs_missing is. A secret_ref_mismatch refusal lists every such name: store the signed values with enterprise secret set (a new value needs enterprise secret set --bundle with the newer bundle that signs it), or sign the bundle again with --secret-file for the stored values. Absent on builds before 1.0.4.

secret_refs.description: Every secret_refs entry of the bundle with its state on this device, in manifest order: name, required, present (the device stores a value) and value_match (the stored value is the one the bundle signs). Names and booleans only, never a value or a digest. Present exactly when secret_refs_missing is. Absent on builds before 1.0.6.

config_drift.description: For result already_applied on a managed device (root or SYSTEM): true when the installed config.yaml is not the confirmed bundle's config (changed or deleted outside the lifecycle). Apply the same bundle again to repair it, scheduled by restart_prediction; with false nothing is to do. Absent for other results, off a device, when the installed config or the bundle store could not be read, and on builds before 1.0.4.

secretRefState.description: enterprisebundle.SecretRefState (internal/enterprisebundle/secrets.go). Every listed entry binds a value: verify refuses an entry that signs only a name (secret_ref_unbound) before it reads the store.

value_match.description: true when the stored value is the value the bundle signs; false when it is another value or nothing is stored.

restartPrediction.description: bundleRestartPrediction (internal/cli/enterprise_bundle_restart.go): whether applying this verified bundle restarts the gateway; managed hooks fail closed while it restarts, so an agent applies a required bundle only in its maintenance window. Computed with the classifier the apply uses on this OS from the installed config.yaml and the bundle config. Present on a managed device for result verified or already_applied when --platform is this OS; absent off a device, on a refusal and on builds before 1.0.3.

gateway_restart.description: required: the apply restarts the gateway (Windows: a Codex protection change restarts every DefenseClaw service). not_required: no changed setting needs a restart, so the gateway keeps running; the apply still restarts a gateway that is down or does not report the new policy in time. unknown: not predictable, see reason_codes.

reason_codes.description: restart_settings: settings lists the restart-required settings; codex_machine_policy (Windows): Codex protection turns on or off, which runs the full lifecycle transaction; fleet_setup_required (Windows): the bundle changes fleet.enabled, which the apply refuses (deliver it through signed Setup); already_applied: the bundle is the confirmed one and the installed config.yaml is its config (config_drift false; a drifted installed config is classified like any other change, and config_drift is true); installed_config_unreadable: the installed config.yaml could not be read (run as root or SYSTEM) or, on Windows, parsed.

settings.description: The restart-required settings the change touches, as setting patterns (guardrail.hook_self_heal, guardrail.connectors.*.enabled, enterprise.enrollment), never concrete change paths, which can carry a profile, group or connector name.

errors.message: bundle version_not_newer: version 12 is not above the floor 12 (the last confirmed bundle)
bundle secret_ref_missing: secret_refs: this device has no credential ai-defense-api-key
